37cb3361428e83b7ce5fae78b711e67adcb314d0.summary: Krebs on Security reports that Microsoft won a U.S. federal court order letting it seize control of a Chinese Internet service provider's network, to take over more than 70,000 domains linked to distributing hundreds of malware strains. Microsoft said more than 35 million unique Internet addresses contacted those domains within hours of the order. The botnet was described as believed to be closely linked to counterfeit Windows sold in China. Experts say the Chinese service has long been associated with espionage attacks against U.S. and European corporations.

37ff61ba7b226723f1edb5e971e6c8b99eba4714.summary: Elastio's analysis page on Fs0ciety Locker ransomware, first seen September 1, 2016. It says the family modifies encrypted files with specific patterns to mark them as encrypted, then displays ransom notes demanding payment for file recovery. Associated files named are driver_update.exe, driver_update[1].exe and Invoice_payment.docm. How it alters file modification timestamps is not known. The page belongs to Elastio's detection database and promotes Elastio's own detection product. Last updated July 13, 2023.

37114c033cf4dc4e27f0631d4af9be712dbea44b.summary: ENKI WhiteHat analyses new Android APK variants of the DOCSWAP malware strain. The apps are distributed through phishing, QR codes and fake delivery and security-app lures, and each embeds an encrypted APK that runs a RAT with keylogging, infostealer and remote-command features. ENKI attributes the activity to DPRK-nexus Kimsuky, citing shared infrastructure, a known phishing string and Korean-language comments. The report could not confirm the initial access vector and assesses smishing or email delivery. It also describes Naver and Kakao phishing proxy sites.

37d087169d2bd363bc461552f900cf1b1f854864.summary: AhnLab ASEC reports that the Andariel attack group used a malicious file to carry out RID Hijacking during breach incidents. RID Hijacking changes an account's Relative Identifier in the SAM registry so that a lower-privilege or hidden account is treated as administrator. The report walks through the stages: SYSTEM privilege escalation using PsExec and JuicyPotato, creating a hidden account, and changing its RID. It describes two malicious files, one custom-built and one based on the open-source CreateHiddenAccount tool, and steps taken to conceal the account. It also cites an earlier KISA…
